Maybe it’s the bucolic setting, in the lee of a wooded hill on the edge of the Chilterns, that does it for me.

Recent findings suggest that the stadium might be modest but the team has a habit of punching above its weight. It’s a great place to go and feel the underdog spirit that is part of the force that drives English football.

Division: League Two Opened: 1878 Capacity: 9,507.

Spotland is a decent little ground in the middle of terraced streets that, I am told, has not lost its gritty character.

I'll still be calling it Spotland.

I haven't been since Rochdale were promoted from the National League in the summer but I have heard that one of the best fish and chip shops in the whole of football is right next to the ground so that's as good an excuse as any for me to get back there quickly.

Sources indicate that the last (and only) time I went was on September 4, 1984, a Tuesday night for a League Cup first round match. The floodlights were dim but Spotland is a decent little ground in the middle of terraced streets that, I am told, has not lost its gritty character.

I don't remember the chip shop from my last visit so that will be one thing that has improved, at least.

Division: League One Opened: 1910 Capacity: 19,841.

Meadow Lane is a wonderful ground to visit and it's evolved into an impressive modern arena.

The first time I went to Meadow Lane, it was to see Manchester United play a top-flight game there.

Industry observers note that the away section was uncovered and the stadium had quirks and character. It’s still a wonderful ground to visit and it has evolved into an impressive modern arena that has plenty of nods to its rich history and its status as one of the founder members of the Football League.

Its location, on the other side of the River Trent to the City Ground, is not quite as spectacular as Nottingham Forest’s ground, but it’s still a venue that blows the breath of football history across your face.

Sources indicate that 44. Highbury Stadium, Fleetwood Town.

Division: League Two Opened: 1939 Capacity: 5,137.

This Highbury may not be quite as august as Arsenal’s old stadium but it has an elegant, modern main stand and a fierce local identity.

Like Leeds, Morecambe and Grimsby Town, going to watch Fleetwood is enhanced by local fish and chips.

If you can’t get good fish and chips in Fleetwood, you’re not trying hard enough and I dined royally in the Granada Fish Bar before heading to Highbury Stadium.

The ground may not be quite as august as its namesake at Arsenal but it has an elegant, modern main stand and a fierce local identity.

Industry observers note that the club’s nickname is The Fishermen and the fans chant a lot about the Cod Army. It’s a great day out by the seaside.

Industry observers note that 43. University of Bradford Stadium, Bradford City.

Division: League One Opened: 1886 Capacity: 24,433.

Bradford's Valley Parade still has its character, and is a fine stadium to visit.

It is impossible to think of Valley Parade without thinking of the tragedy that befell Bradford City in 1985 when its main stand was engulfed by flames and 56 people lost their lives.

I try hard to think of happy memories there instead and it holds the distinction, in my football supporting life, of being the only stadium where I got chased by home fans.

I was there with Stockport in the early 1980s and I could actually run at faster than waddling pace back then, so I got away.

Valley Parade still has its character, it is still a fine stadium to visit. Every trip there is a chance to remember those who were lost.

Division: League Two Opened: 2013 Capacity: 6,500.

The Hive flirts with soullessness but just about evades it. For a start it’s one of the only stadiums that allows you to watch the action, fleetingly, from the London Underground.

The Hive flirts with soullessness but just about evades it.

For a start it’s one of the only stadiums that allows you to watch the action, fleetingly, from the London Underground.

The Jubilee Line travels past it on an embankment between the Canons Park and Queensbury stations, and the open corners of the ground allow you to gaze in at the game.

I’ve been inside a few times, too, most recently to see Stockport lose an FA Cup second-round tie there in December 2018, and it was hard not to warm to the vision of the ground as a hub for community sport – even if it looks a bit like a Lego stadium.

Recent findings suggest that 41. The Valley, Charlton Athletic.

Division: Championship Opened: 1919 Capacity: 27,111.

There is still something magical about The Valley, even if it has changed out of all recognition from its glory days.

The Valley has changed out of all recognition from the glory days when more than 75,000 crammed into it in the 1930s.

But there is still something magical about the home of Charlton Athletic. Perhaps, for those of us who are old enough, it is the memory of the old East Terrace rising up towards the south London sky. Even when it was crumbling and condemned, there was something majestic about it, something that recalled great days.

Perhaps, too, there is something about the knowledge of how hard the fans fought, for seven years in the late 80s and early 90s, to return to the stadium when it seemed it had been ripped away from them.

And even if only that memory of the old East Terrace remains now, the walk down into the valley where the revamped stadium nestles still feels like a journey to the heart of the English game.

Industry observers note that 40. Mornflake Stadium, Crewe Alexandra.

Division: League Two Opened: 1906 Capacity: 10,109.

Gresty Road is a better stadium now than it was in 1983, which isn’t a high bar, and it has a better owner than it did then.

I have got a lot of affection for Gresty Road. On a Friday night at the end of September 1983, it was where I saw Micky Quinn score a hat-trick for Stockport County at the home of our bitter rivals.

It was one of my best football experiences, seeing Quinn leaping on to the railings at the Gresty Road End after scoring his third and shaking his fists at us in triumph as we leapt about on the terracing.

If there was footage of the fans’ wild celebrations now, the caption might say ‘limbs’.

Gresty Road is a better stadium now than it was then (which isn’t a high bar) and it has a better owner than it did then. But it can’t be easy living in the shadow of such mighty neighbours.

39. SMH Group Stadium, Chesterfield.

Division: League Two Opened: 2010 Capacity: 10,400.

I loved the old ground at Saltergate but when the club moved to the upcoming stadium and called it the b2net Stadium, it felt as if it had sold its soul.

Industry observers note that I used to have a bit of a vendetta against the SMH Group Stadium. Perhaps not a vendetta, but certainly a prejudice.

Sources indicate that I loved the old ground at Saltergate but when the club moved to the newly introduced stadium and called it the b2net Stadium, it felt as if it had sold its soul. Since 2009, it has also been called the Proact Stadium and the Technique Stadium.

In a recent development, but getting to know a club sometimes changes your view of a place. I spent a bit of time there last season when I went to watch Kieron Dyer, who was a coach at the club, and Paul Cook, the manager, at work.

I met the owners, who are local businessmen and clearly have the club’s best interests at heart, and took in a game. Suddenly the SMH Group Stadium had new life and character and soul breathed into it for me. It’s a club on the up and it’s a club that cares about its fans, and so my prejudice against the SMH Group Stadium is no more.

38. Boundary Park, Oldham Athletic.

Division: League Two Opened: 1904 Capacity: 13,186.

Boundary Park is not the most beautiful of stadiums but it’s got some grand old character and it’s embedded at the heart of its community.

In a recent development, I remember the cold at Boundary Park. I think a lot of people do.

For a long time, I laboured under the misapprehension that it was the highest ground in the Football League when, in fact, that distinction belongs to the Hawthorns.

Boundary Park just feels like it should be the highest. It’s not the most beautiful of stadiums but it’s got some grand old character and it’s embedded at the heart of its community.

It just so happens some of my best friends are Oldham fans, too, so I was delighted when they came up from the National League in 2025. It’s a treat to have the ground back in the 92.

Division: League One Opened: 1950 Capacity: 15,036.

I’ve got a soft spot for Vale Park - it was the first away ground I ever went to.

I’ve got a soft spot for Vale Park.

It was the first away ground I ever went to and I still remember the excitement of planning the train journey from Stockport, making it to Burslem and getting a thrill out of the entirely different experience – the extra camaraderie – that being an away fan at another club’s ground brings.

Vale Park felt raw and real to me back then and it got even better on my next visit when, in Stockport’s final year in the Football League before relegation to the National League, Anthony Elding got the winner for County in the 87th minute in front of the away end.

It was beautiful mayhem. County were relegated a few weeks later but I’ll never forget those days at Vale Park.

It has been revealed that 36. Toughsheet Community Stadium, Bolton Wanderers.

Division: Championship Opened: 1997 Capacity: 28,018.

This is one of the earliest, and best, of the new generation of stadiums, and even if it is on the outskirts of Bolton, its bold design makes it a local landmark.

When it was the Macron Stadium, one of its several previous incarnations, I interviewed Tyson Fury there - and he threatened to have my jaw broken.

When it was the Macron Stadium, one of its several previous incarnations, I interviewed Tyson Fury in a room at the hotel that was part of the Toughsheet Community Stadium in the build-up to his world title fight with Wladimir Klitschko.

After he’d claimed the Klitschkos were part of a devil-worshipping ring, Fury made some rather unpleasant comments about his views on links between homosexuality and paedophilia.

Recent findings suggest that when the interview was printed, he did not seem best pleased with the results. He said his brother, Big Shane, was going to break my jaw ‘completely’ with a straight right hand.

‘See big Shane there?’ Fury said. ‘Have a look at big Shane. He’s 6ft 6in and 25st. He’s going to break (your) jaw completely with one straight right hand. I ain’t going to do it, ‘cos I’ll get in trouble. But the big fella, there – he’ll annihilate (you), won’t he? So Oliver, take a good look at him, because that’s the face you’re going to see before you hit the deck.’.

Fun times. I’ve never found quite the same level of excitement in watching Bolton Wanderers there, although it had some great days in the 2000s when it was called the Reebok and Sam Allardyce was the manager.

It is one of the earliest, and best, of the newly introduced generation of stadiums, and even if it is on the outskirts of the town, its bold design makes it a local landmark.

Division: Championship Opened: 1899 Capacity: 20,899.

Fratton Park has not lost the intensity and the raucousness that makes it such a hostile place to visit for opposing teams.

Since Luton Town's brief sojourn in the Premier League, everyone has become aware of the entrances to their Kenilworth Road ground, through what appears to be the ground floor of a terraced house.

But the old way in to Fratton Park, beneath a half-timbered gable, is even more charming.

One of the old institutions of English football, the stadium has been renovated but has not lost the intensity and the raucousness that makes it such a hostile place to visit for opposing teams.

Division: Premier League Opened: 1884 Capacity: 29,813.

Portman Road is still a wonderful stadium, a ground at the centre of its community, where you can breathe in the legends of Sir Alf Ramsey and Sir Bobby Robson.

In a recent development, the matchday hospitality of the Cobbolds, the former owners of Ipswich Town, was legendary amongst journalists. I missed out on those days but a visit to Portman Road is still a treat.

It is still a wonderful ground, a ground at the centre of its community, a ground where you can breathe in the legends of Sir Alf Ramsey and Sir Bobby Robson, great football men who did great things in their time in charge of the club.

A few years ago, I went to the launch of Kieron Dyer’s autobiography in a suite at the stadium and it was a night that underlined how crucial the club is to the town.

According to recent reports, it is a joy to see that the current hierarchy value the importance of the stadium and have lavished care and money on it. It is one of the great outposts of the English game.

33. Molineux, Wolverhampton Wanderers.

Division: Championship Opened: 1889 Capacity: 31,750.

Molineux is a stadium whose four stands are named after club legends and previous owner and benefactor Sir Jack Hayward, and which takes care to respect its glorious past.

When I first started going to Molineux, it was dominated by a peculiarity.

One of the stands, the John Ireland Stand as it was then, was about 100ft from the touchline, a matter of much mirth for visiting fans.

It has been renamed the Steve Bull Stand now and the pitch has been repositioned so that the modern Molineux is a stadium that makes sense.

It is an arena to be proud of again for Wolves fans, a stadium whose four stands are named after club legends and previous owner and benefactor Sir Jack Hayward, and which takes care to respect its glorious past.

Division: Championship Opened: 1883 Capacity: 21,990.

Turf Moor is a wonderful place to watch football, where you can gaze out over the town and its mills.

Turf Moor is a wonderful place to watch football.

Sit in the North Stand, opposite the Bob Lord Stand, and you can gaze out over the town and its mills, which do not look quite as dark and satanic any more, and remember that you are in the traditional northern heartlands of our game here.

I have a friend from Burnley who insists that more people per head wear the jersey of their hometown club in Burnley than in any other football centre in England.

This is a club, after all, that may be bouncing between the Premier League and Championship now but which won the league title in 1921 and 1960 and was once a giant of the game here.

Stoke seems to have been put on a pedestal for thier ability to provide a hostile environment for visiting teams – but Turf Moor can serve up the weather and the atmosphere to run it close.

31. The Hawthorns, West Bromwich Albion.

Division: Championship Opened: 1900 Capacity: 26,688.

The Hawthorns is the highest league ground in England, sitting on its perch above the M5, and it is also one of football’s great theatres.

I have seen a few crackers at The Hawthorns.

The 5-5 draw between West Brom and Manchester United in May 2013 that was Sir Alex Ferguson’s last game as a manager is probably top of the list.

Sources indicate that I was in the press room there in May 2017 when Chelsea sealed the title under Antonio Conte and the players invaded his press conference to shower him in champagne and generally rough him up. Conte did not look best pleased.

The highest league ground in England, sitting on its perch above the M5, it is also one of football’s great theatres, a ground where the support exudes a love for the game and a warmth that survives the vicissitudes of the club’s fortunes on the pitch.

30. Cledara Abbey Stadium, Cambridge United.

Division: League One Opened: 1932 Capacity: 8,024.

Cambridge might be in League One but the noise inside the Abbey Stadium would have put plenty of Premier League grounds to shame.

I made it to the Abbey Stadium for the first time on New Year's Day 2025 for the game against Reading.

I walked to the ground down Cut Throat Lane and stood on the terraces at the Newmarket Road End where the singing is at its loudest and where the names and shirts of the celebrated early 1990s team of John Beck, which included Dion Dublin, are painted on the wall at the back of the stand.

Cambridge might be in League One but the noise inside would have put plenty of Premier League grounds to shame.

29. Deepdale, Preston North End.

Division: Championship Opened: 1878 Capacity: 23,404.

I love going to Deepdale just for the history. Just to gaze down from the stands and know this is where Tom Finney once played is enough to make it a memorable experience.

And the sense of it being a pilgrimage is only enhanced by the fact that one of the best statues in football sits outside the ground.

I love going to Deepdale just for the history of the place. Just to gaze down from the stands and know that this was where Tom Finney once played is enough to make it a memorable experience.

And the sense of it being a pilgrimage is only enhanced by the fact that one of the best statues in football sits outside the ground.

Taking its inspiration from the 1956 sports photo of the year, which showed Finney aquaplaning through a huge puddle at Stamford Bridge, the sculpture, known as The Splash, immortalises Finney outside his hometown club.

It’s a wonderful tribute outside an arena redolent with memories of one of England’s greatest players.

It has been revealed that 28. Kenilworth Road, Luton Town.

Division: League One Opened: 1905 Capacity: 10,265.

Luton will move to a latest stadium at Power Court in the city centre in a few years but Kenilworth Road will be missed.

The stadium entrance goes straight through the middle of a row of terraced houses.

The first time I went to Kenilworth Road was 43 years ago. I stood on the open terrace that hosted the away fans for an FA Cup fourth round tie that Manchester United won 2-0.

The most recent time I went was in November 2021, to see Neil Warnock break the record for the most games managed in English football but unable to stop his Middlesbrough team falling to a 3-1 defeat.

Across those decades, the atmosphere at the old stadium has endured. The Main Stand, which is more than a hundred years old, shook that night as Luton took Boro down and the stadium became a bear pit.

Sources indicate that it attained a kind of fame all over again when the club’s return to the top flight recently focused attention on the quirky Oak Road End entrance that goes straight through the middle of a row of terraced houses. Luton will move to a new stadium at Power Court in the city centre in a few years but Kenilworth Road will be missed.

Sources indicate that 27. Etihad Stadium, Manchester City.

Division: Premier League Opened: 2002 Capacity: 61,038.

The Etihad is this high on the list because it’s witnessed one of the best teams in English football history - even if that all feels a little tainted now.

I’d probably have Maine Road in the top three in this list if Manchester City still played there. I loved that ground. I loved the benches in the Platt Lane stand, I loved standing on the Kippax, I loved the cantilever Main Stand and the alleyways around the ground and walking across Platt Fields to the game.

Recent findings suggest that but the Etihad isn’t Maine Road. It’s this high on the list because it’s in Manchester and it’s witnessed one of the best teams in English football history playing on its turf, marshalled by one of the game’s great managers – even if all that feels a little tainted by City's guilty verdict in their case with the Premier League, subject to appeal.

City have done their best to breathe personality into it but it’s hard to disguise the fact it’s a characterless, identikit modern stadium.

The corporate denizens of the Tunnel Club, traipsing back to their seats well after the whistle has blown for the start of the second half, don’t help, either.

26. Rodney Parade, Newport County.

Division: League Two Opened: 1877 Capacity: 8,722.

Not far from the banks of the River Usk, it’s a modern stadium with remnants of character that come into its own when the giants come to play for the FA Cup.

A Cardiff taxi driver once told me that the best fights in Wales happen outside Newport railway station late on Saturday nights. He said he sometimes took a break just to go and watch the action.

Rodney Parade’s a fine place to watch sport, too. Not far from the banks of the River Usk, it’s a modern stadium with remnants of character that come into its own when the giants come to play in the FA Cup.

I was there a few years ago when Manchester City visited in the fifth round and after the game, the way out for fans took them past the open windows of the small changing rooms behind one of the goals where you could hear the celebrations of Pep Guardiola’s team booming out into the South Wales night.

Like the railway station, it’s not a place for the faint-hearted.

25. Nigel Eady County Ground, Swindon Town.

Division: League Two Opened: 1892 Capacity: 15,547.

Recent findings suggest that my most recent trip to the County Ground was a 0-0 draw with Accrington Stanley last year. It wasn’t the best game but I had the best time.

There were more than 20 years between my first visit to the County Ground and my most recent, a 0-0 draw with Accrington Stanley in March 2025. It wasn’t the best game but I had the best time.

I’d had a week of being abused on social media by Newcastle fans (which is part of the job and, yes, I agree, I don’t have to read it) and going to Swindon felt like a wonderful breeze blowing on my face.

Sources indicate that for a start, there were more than 7,000 supporters there, for a fourth-tier game which meant nothing to both teams in terms of promotion or relegation. The atmosphere was lively and passionate and the ground has character and warmth, even if one of the ends was closed.

According to recent reports, at half-time, I watched a DS Active match between lads with Down Syndrome representing Swindon and Bristol City and it was a joy. It was a joy to see their uncomplicated joy in the beauty of football and the way they celebrated their goals and their skill and the way they looked for their parents in the stands when they scored and the way they supported their team-mates.

It has been revealed that the match was a reminder of what it means for a football club to be at the heart of its community. A stadium is about more than just a game.

In a recent development, 24. American Express Stadium, Brighton & Hove Albion.

Division: Premier League Opened: 2011 Capacity: 31,876.

Maybe it is the knowledge of where Brighton & Hove Albion came from to get here that makes a visit to the Amex Stadium such an uplifting thing.

Maybe it is the knowledge of where Brighton & Hove Albion came from to get here that makes a visit to the Amex Stadium such an uplifting thing.

I remember seeing them at the Goldstone Ground, which I loved, but also at the Withdean Stadium, which is a glorified parks pitch inside a small athletics stadium.

When you have commuted to ‘home’ games at Gillingham’s Priestfield Stadium for two years as well, it is little wonder the Amex still feels like the promised land.

Neat on the inside, bold on the outside, it is a fitting home for an exceptionally well-run club and a fanbase that never gave up on its team.

In a recent development, 23. Gtech Community Stadium, Brentford.

Division: Premier League Opened: 2020 Capacity: 17,250.

Brentford pulled off an architectural wonder with the Gtech, squeezing it into a parcel of land in the shadow of the raised section of the M4 in west London.

It is not often one of the upcoming-build generation of English football stadiums has more character than a club’s former ground but the Gtech Community Stadium is a happy exception.

Griffin Park was much beloved, of course, and its peculiar feature of boasting a pub at each of the four corners of the ground was part of the game’s folklore. But Brentford pulled off an architectural wonder with the Gtech, squeezing it into a parcel of land in the shadow of the raised section of the M4 in west London.

The club has frequently had one of the best home records in the Premier League since coming up in 2021, which is testimony not just to the excellence of the players and manager but to the tight confines of the ground and the atmosphere it creates.

In a recent development, it is no surprise it is attracting supporters who previously considered themselves without an affiliation. It is the type of stadium, and club, that makes fans feel they belong.

Division: Championship Opened: 1801 Capacity: 10,500.

I’m not one of those who regards the Ryan Reynolds/Rob McElhenney takeover of Wrexham with distaste.

I went to a lot of games in Wrexham in the late 70s and early 80s. My best mate, Bryn, was from the town so when his mum and dad took him to visit family there, I went along and we headed for the Racecourse Ground.

I’m not one of those who regards the Ryan Reynolds/Rob McElhenney takeover of the club with distaste, although I am aware that my friend and colleague Ian Herbert, a Wrexham fan and a club scholar, has had some misgivings.

Nothing in football is ever quite as wholesome as it seems but so far, it feels as if it has been good for the club and for the town.

I don’t know what their long-term motives are but they have poured a lot of money into the team and into the infrastructure, and the club has risen and risen through the leagues. It’s bringing more light into a community that has had its share of hard times.

I was at the Racecourse, by the way, when Mark Hughes scored his spectacular overhead kick against Spain in 1985. It’s still one of the top five goals I’ve ever seen live.

(The others: Angel Di Maria for Argentina at the Lusail Stadium in the 2022 World Cup final, Zlatan Ibrahimovic for Sweden against England at the Friends Arena in 2012, Dennis Bergkamp for the Netherlands against Argentina at the Stade Velodrome at France '98 and Norman Whiteside for Manchester United against Everton at Wembley in the 1985 FA Cup final).

21. St Andrew's, Birmingham City.

Division: Championship Opened: 1906 Capacity: 29,409.

There are wealthy owners at Birmingham now, of course, and major plans, but St Andrew’s is still at the heart of everything.

Down the winding stairs from the press box, though the main reception area where staff are trying to sort ticket requests, through the foyer, down another set of steps and into a tunnel below the Main Stand where four garden forks hang on the wall outside the groundsman’s room – St Andrew’s is still a beautiful stadium that mixes old-school elements and modern stands.

It’s a great place to watch a game. If it gets overshadowed by Aston Villa and West Brom, it still feels as if the soul of the Second City is alive in this place.

There are wealthy owners now, of course, and big aims, but St Andrew’s is still at the heart of everything.

Recent findings suggest that 20. Stadium of Light, Sunderland.

Division: Premier League Opened: 1997 Capacity: 48,095.

Sunderland have some of the best supporters in the country and the noise the fans make when the biggest occasions present themselves is up there with anyone.

Recent findings suggest that I loved Roker Park. Like Maine Road, I’d have it in my top 10 grounds if Sunderland were still playing there now and I feel lucky to have stood in the away end there and been treated to the full force of the Roker Roar.

Sources indicate that I’ve never been quite sure what to make of its successor, the Stadium of Light. I’m not even sure about the name, which is dramatic, certainly, but is also an obvious copy of the original Benfica ground in Lisbon – which opened in 1954 and held 130,000 at its peak.

Recent findings suggest that the design is rather uninspiring for such an evocative name, too. It’s uncomfortably close to identikit fresh-build, but I have friends who say it’s their favourite anywhere.

The stadium does sit proudly atop the bluffs of the River Wear and it’s wonderful to see the team on the up again and back in the Premier League. These are some of the best supporters in the country and the noise the fans make when the biggest occasions present themselves is up there with anyone.

19. Bramall Lane, Sheffield United.

Division: Championship Opened: 1855 Capacity: 32,050.

Bramall Lane's Kop singing the Greasy Chip Butty song is one of the iconic experiences in English football.

Bramall Lane is still the only ground where I’ve sat in the dugout during a league game.

According to recent reports, neil Warnock is a friend of mine and when he was in charge at Sheffield United, he let me sit next to him in an end-of-season Championship game against Ipswich Town. I got a front row seat for Rob Kozluk, one of the game’s great sledgers, doing his best to wind up then-Ipswich boss Joe Royle.

I can’t think of many better grounds to have had the privilege. Bramall Lane is a cauldron of noise, full of history and passion, in the heart of the city.

Its Kop singing the Greasy Chip Butty song is one of the iconic experiences in English football.

Division: Premier League Opened: 1877 Capacity: 40,044.

All stadiums change and modernise with the years but there are few stadiums which have changed as dramatically as Stamford Bridge.

All stadiums change and modernise with the years but there are few stadiums which have changed as dramatically as Stamford Bridge.

It was once an intimidating place, dominated by the Shed, a sprawling, boisterous semi-circular terrace behind one of the goals that was synonymous with the crowd problems of the 1970s and early 80s.

Going to watch a Chelsea game now is an entirely different experience. The transformation began under Ken Bates, one of a group of visionary businessmen who changed the way we watch football, and then continued under Roman Abramovich.

And now, for many, going to Chelsea, with its towering West Stand and opulent corporate boxes, is a boutique experience not out of place with the hugely affluent area in which it stands.

You can still feel the history of the place when you visit, though. To its credit, the club preserved the original wall that stood at the back of the Shed and it remains in place, used to display pictures of Chelsea legends.

Maybe I should declare a certain bias here, too: the food in the press room at the Bridge is the best in the Premier League.

Industry observers note that 17. Selhurst Park, Crystal Palace.

Division: Premier League Opened: 1924 Capacity: 25,194.

A trip to Crystal Palace's Selhurst Park is one of the best experiences in the English game.

Recent findings suggest that I used to be put off by what I saw, pathetically, as the difficulty of getting to Selhurst Park in south London. Difficult to drive to, hard to find a parking space, not on the Tube, etc, etc.

I got over that some time ago. A trip to Palace is one of the best experiences in the English game.

The atmosphere generated by the Holmesdale Road stand, in particular, makes Selhurst Park one of the best grounds in England to watch football.

Other clubs have seen the volume of their support dim as the demographic of their fans has changed but that has not happened at Selhurst Park. It is one of the few places left that has the power to intimidate and it is all the better for that.

It has been revealed that 16. MATRADE Loftus Road, Queens Park Rangers.

Division: Championship Opened: 1904 Capacity: 18,193.

One of the great surviving community grounds, a beautiful, steep-sided gem of a boutique stadium in Shepherd’s Bush, Loftus Road is a place to cherish.

One of the great surviving community grounds, a beautiful, steep-sided gem of a boutique stadium in Shepherd’s Bush, Loftus Road is a place to cherish.

In a recent development, when Bernie Ecclestone was a part-owner of the club, I sat in the directors’ box with him a few times and got shushed by Flavio Briatore for talking too much when my neighbour kept asking me questions. That may have been the first time anybody has ever been accused of talking more than Flavio.

The football wasn’t the best during their time there but the hospitality was: they had Mayfair restaurant Cipriani doing the catering.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Milan are expected to sell Pervis Estupinan and Ruben Loftus-Cheek in the January transfer window, with Turkish and English clubs interested, while Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto are heading on loan.

The Rossoneri have stuttered so far this season and found significant differences between the first choice team’s performance and those who come in during squad rotation.

This has prompted three defeats out of four Europa League games so far, and coach Ruben Amorim is reportedly ready to cut some players loose.

Amorim had declared at the start of the season that he convinced Milan to keep hold of Estupinan when a move to Aston Villa had been practically agreed.

Now several months on, he seemingly regrets that decision and has given the all-clear for an exit, but the Premier League side is no longer interested.

A loan move to Fiorentina could be on the cards, although they hope to find a more permanent solution to make back some of that investment.

Loftus-Cheek is only under contract with the Rossoneri until the end of this season, but persistent injuries and poor performances should see him sold in January.

Coventry City had made an approach in the summer, and could well try again, but Besiktas and other Turkish teams are also options.

Meanwhile, young players Camarda and Comotto are clearly not going to get a chance to deliver, so will be sent out on loan in January to gain valuable experience.

Genoa are the most advanced in talks for midfielder Comotto, while Camarda has numerous proposals from Serie A, B, and even abroad.

Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (420 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hungary on Thursday stated it would ease abortion rules and ratify an international treaty on violence against women.
  • Under the planned changes to the so-called "heartbeat regulation," women will no longer be forced to listen to the vital signs of the fetus before an abortion.
  • Women will also be able to get emergency contraceptive pills without prescription.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hungary on Thursday stated it would ease abortion rules and ratify an international treaty on violence against women.

Under the planned changes to the so-called "heartbeat regulation," women will no longer be forced to listen to the vital signs of the fetus before an abortion.

Women will also be able to get emergency contraceptive pills without prescription.

The changes proposed by the newly introduced government under Prime Minister Peter Magyar are a significant break with the conservative policies of his predecessor Viktor Orban.

The country also prepares to ratify the Istanbul Convention, a treaty aimed at preventing violence against women and domestic violence.

Hungarian law allows for most abortions to be performed up to 12 weeks, and up to 24 weeks in cases of severe developmental abnormalities. Until now, women were required to have a medical provider show them evidence of a definitive sign of fetal life, commonly understood as the so-called "fetal heartbeat," before deciding whether to have an abortion.

The controversial 2022 policy had received widespread criticism from doctors and women’s rights groups as being cruel and humiliating. It will now be scrapped.

The policy had not led to a decline in abortions and according to Magyar, had raised "serious bioethical questions.".

The second major change is that emergency contraception will be available without prescription.

Further measures include changing the criminal code aimed at better protecting women, including making the misuse of intimate images a criminal offense and strengthening the treatment of victims of domestic violence during criminal proceedings.

Hungary also plans to ratify an international treaty on the protection of women which most other EU members have long ratified. The Istanbul Convention came into force in 2014 and, among other things, requires rape to be criminalized based on the absence of freely given consent.

"We are making it clear that sexual acts can only ⁠take ​place with the voluntary consent of the other party," ​Magyar remarked.

The government of his predecessor Orban had opposed the treaty, arguing that it promoted what it described as "gender ideology.".

"We are making a clear and accountable commitment to putting an end to the era of inaction," Magyar said in a Facebook video.

Among the EU’s other members, only Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Lithuania and Slovakia have not yet ratified the convention.

The Istanbul Convention is a treaty by the Council of Europe, an international organization that promotes human rights and the rule of law across Europe and includes more countries than the member of the EU.

Effective networking does not come naturally to everyone. Credit: sanjeri/Getty.

Sources indicate that networking is not “random socializing”, says Nessa Carey. It’s a professional skill that can be learnt and developed.

Carey, a UK-based entrepreneur and consultant, explains in a six-minute video why scientists often struggle with networking, drawing on her own experiences while working in industry and academia.

Recent findings suggest that both Carey and Caroline Dunne, an academic careers coach based in the United Kingdom and Australia, describe how to identify good people to chat to, ask insightful opening questions and circulate effectively in a room packed with strangers. In her six-minute video, Dunne recommends arriving early and indicates it is fine to leave an event before it formally ends.

The two videos formed part of a session on networking at Nature’s flagship Reframing Precision Medicine conference in London last month.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

David Moyes was presented with a commemorative frame ahead of Monday night’s Premier League away fixture against Brentford – a record-breaking match for the Everton manager.

The trip to the Gtech Community Stadium will mark Moyes’ 593rd game as Everton manager, taking him ahead of the legendary Harry Catterick in the all-time rankings.

Everton captain James Tarkowski and former Blues midfielder Leon Osman were on hand to present the signed frame – and Moyes mentioned it’s a “privilege and honour” to have reached the historic milestone.

In a recent development, "I'm really thrilled about. I've become the manager who has managed more Everton games than anyone before. That's a privilege and an honour to be put in that position.

It has been revealed that "I have to thank the people who brought me to the Club in the first place. When you take a chance on a young manager, you never know it'll be work, but they had great faith and believed in me.

"I'm so thankful for the people around Everton because they've been so good for me.".

Industry observers note that handing over the frame, Osman remarked: “It’s a record I don’t think will ever be beaten – and I don’t say that lightly. This is some achievement for a huge football club.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m sure James is like me in saying it’s been an honour to play for you. It’s been an honour, a privilege. It’s been hard! But you’ve made us all better and we wish you many more successes for the upcoming seasons.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of vital saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

Recent findings suggest that alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

Industry observers note that zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk.

Suzuki appeared to have been put off by the presence of Fulham’s Shea Charles, but Emery refused to single out the player for criticism.

Sources indicate that “I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager mentioned. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

Industry observers note that “I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

Industry observers note that “We have to change our mind quickly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”.

Recent findings suggest that villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

In a recent development, it was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

Industry observers note that mcGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”.

Penalty MISSED! John McGinn hits the bar 💥 https://t.co/2kBYkYA2BY.

Nicolas Jackson was on hand to ease Villa’s nerves before the break, though. the Villa manager had said before the game that the striker’s goalscoring capability meant he was capable of matching the likes of Harry Kane. His assessment was backed up by Jackson scoring the opening goal, after 40 minutes, which summed up the striker in one moment of pure power combined with agility.

Collecting Johan Manzambi’s superbly weighted pass, Jackson forced his way past two defenders before sliding in the goal that put Villa ahead.

Emery’s touchline celebrations said it all as the Senegal forward continues to flourish under the man who knew how to get the best out of him at Villarreal.

Nicolas Jackson scores his fifth league goal in five games! 🔥 https://t.co/W0xmFtW1Gt.

Suzuki has also flourished under Emery and he kept Villa in the game with some superb saves.

Recent findings suggest that when Antonee Robinson crossed for Gonzalo Garcia, his step over allowed Oscar Bobb in for what looked like his second goal in successive games. But Suzuki pulled off a stunning fingertip save. That had Villa supporters singing: “Zion Suzuki, the world’s No 1”.

Robinson put in another cross and Suzuki got a touch that was enough to make Garcia put his shot wide. Villa were living dangerously and the Japanese goalkeeper made another outstanding stop to keep out Iwobi’s header. But then it all went wrong for Suzuki when he fumbled Iwobi’s corner.

That allowed Fulham’s recent revival under manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, to continue – they now have seven points from their past three games.

“We spoke at half-time about what we had to do,” Arbeloa said. “If you want to win a game you have to fight and I think we have to believe in our way, we’ve shown we can beat anyone in the way that we play but we have to be aggressive.

“We created so many chances and at the end it’s one point in a difficult stadium. I’m so happy with the second half because of the way we played, this is the team that we want to be.”.

"This is the first time I've seen him that little bit confused" Rob Green analyses Zion Suzuki's error that lead to Fulham's equaliser 🔍 https://t.co/B3HCivNpwz.

"I don't think he gets the flowers he deserves" 💐 Jamie Redknapp is a fan of Calvin Bassey 🫡 https://t.co/R9uravAzRU.

It has been revealed that “We started the game well. Fulham are a good side, not easy to win [against] but we came in front. We did well but in the second half we gave them more time on the ball. They have good players and they can make chances. We were unlucky with the goal but we tried to keep fighting. It is crucial not to lose these games.”.

On Zion Suzuki’s mistake for Fulham’s equaliser:.

In a recent development, “It is frustrating because we do not want to concede goals but it can happen to everyone. Zion is a great guy, great goalkeeper. He will learn from it. We will support him and go again.”.

"We should have got more" Calvin Bassey believes Fulham should have came away with three points against Aston Villa ⤵️ https://t.co/pMTMtc4zjS.

Zion Suzuki had big gloves to fill this summer after the sale of Emiliano Martínez but already appears one of the Premier League signings of the summer.

Aston Villa’s fresh No 1 epitomises the vibrant energy of Unai Emery’s revamped squad and is a goalkeeper perfectly suited to the modern game.

The Japanese international is Villa’s own version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson, who revolutionised English football with a vast range of passing from his own penalty area.

Of all the daft statements to have come out of Aston Villa – and I am including Doug Ellis’s frequent claims that he invented the bicycle kick – it is hard to think of anything as absurd as suing a pundit for speaking the truth.

Jamie Carragher’s common-sense declaration that Villa manager Unai Emery might consider a move to Manchester United – because it is a bigger club – has apparently inflicted such a deep wound to the self-esteem of Nassef Sawiris, the chairman, that he has initiated a legal complaint.

According to recent reports, sawiris’s short statement, which he published on social media on Friday night, consisted of 37 ill-chosen words. It started by accusing Carragher of “unacceptable insults to the club and its fans”, then concluded with the vainglorious declaration that “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football”.

Aston Villa manager, Unai Emery, is giving a full Premier League debut to Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka against Fulham this evening.

The 31-year-old joined Villa on a free transfer in the summer, but a knee injury prevented him from making an appearance off the bench until this month’s Champions League tie against Fenerbahce.

Asked what role Goretzka would have with Villa, Emery deadpanned: “The first one is to be available to play.”.

Industry observers note that emery had also made a cryptic remark about Nicolas Jackson and Johann Manzambi in his Friday press conference. The suggestion was that they had been merely rested for Wednesday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Bournemouth.

But the Spaniard noted: “For different reasons, not only rest.”.

Whatever he meant is unclear, but both start for Villa tonight.

Fulham have won their last two league games – against Hull and Coventry.

Manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, has made one change with Sander Berge replacing Hugo Larsson in midfield.

Sources indicate that villa are aiming to win three successive league games for the first time in this calendar year. The omens are good as they’ve beaten Fulham in their last seven league meetings at Villa Park.

Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”.

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

Industry observers note that “It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa mentioned. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

It has been revealed that “They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”.

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

Conte on Chelsea success story, meeting Kante and Fabregas destiny

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Antonio Conte reveals what changed to win the Premier League at Chelsea, the Arsenal player that ‘killed’ them, his funny reaction to meeting N’Golo Kante, and why Cesc Fabregas was ‘destined’ to be a coach.
  • The coach is currently waiting for his next role, after walking away from Napoli with the Scudetto and Supercoppa Italiana in his two seasons at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.
  • He sat down with the Cronache di Spogliatoio podcast and discussed his long career as a coach, including the experience at Chelsea from 2016 to 2018.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Antonio Conte reveals what changed to win the Premier League at Chelsea, the Arsenal player that ‘killed’ them, his funny reaction to meeting N’Golo Kante, and why Cesc Fabregas was ‘destined’ to be a coach.

The coach is currently waiting for his next role, after walking away from Napoli with the Scudetto and Supercoppa Italiana in his two seasons at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

He sat down with the Cronache di Spogliatoio podcast and discussed his long career as a coach, including the experience at Chelsea from 2016 to 2018.

In that spell at Stamford Bridge, he won the Premier League title immediately, then the FA Cup, but admits it required a radical rethink of his Juventus tactics.

“I had this sort of 3-3-4 formation at Juventus, so when I went to Chelsea, I started with the idea of a 4-2-4 formation, but we didn’t have the players at that moment to make it work,” said Conte.

“I had Diego Costa, Eden Hazard, Wilian and Pedro as the wide men, and Oscar as a second striker, so I used a 4-2-3-1 with all of them and kept some of the same movements.

Industry observers note that “We had started well, but after every game I told the staff, we are winning, but I don’t feel this is my team. We were top of the table, but after the break for international duty we took on Francesco Guidolin’s Swansea and it was chaos.

“Anything could’ve happened, it was 2-2, but when there is a sense of instability, these are not my teams. I need sides who control the game. I felt that I didn’t have complete control.”.

The turning point came from a painful defeat to local rivals Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that “It was my first season in the Premier League, but there were Pep Guardiola, Jurgen Klopp, Jose Mourinho, all the best managers. We lost 2-1 at home to Liverpool, then were 3-0 down at half-time to Arsenal.

“Hector Bellerin was killing us down the left, it was one of the few times I was ashamed,” mentioned Conte on the Italian language podcast.

“I realised that was the time I had to change, because I needed to give more protection to Oscar.

It has been revealed that “I put Ivanovic on the right with David Luiz and Cahill, Azpilicueta on the right, basically a 3-4-3. It was the turning point, as the next game against Hull City I put Azpilicueta in the back three, he is a soldier and works wherever you put him, and Moses who Chelsea had wanted to sell.”.

Conte also revealed that some of the meetings with Chelsea players didn’t quite go as planned, but they worked out in the end.

Sources indicate that “It was not a transfer session worthy of Chelsea. Kante had won the Premier League title with Leicester City, I asked for two players, Wanyama and Kante. I’d seen Kante play several times, with him it was as if we were playing with 12 or 13, he never felt tired.

“He walked in behind his agent, I couldn’t even see him. Kante is not a tall man, but he looked like a child, with this big smile. I thought, I expected him to be taller….

Recent findings suggest that “I hoped I hadn’t made a mistake asking for this player, the Premier League they were all huge and physically strong, but the fear only lasted a minute. I spoke to him, Kante is one of the best players I ever coached, and an exceptional lad.”.

Conte reveals the aim at Chelsea that season was for a top 10 finish, but they ended up winning the Premier League.

Industry observers note that “We won 13 games in a row, that is when I felt this was my team, it was in control. Before that, playing three at the back was practically blasphemous in England, but now it has become a cult and many teams do it.”.

Cesc Fabregas was in that Chelsea team too, and has now gone on to become a coach in his own right at Como, qualifying for the Champions League.

“His curiosity, his desire to learn, to modify, Cesc was destined for greatness,” insisted Conte.

“He was a thinker on the field too, so that helped. He could see the move before he got the ball, was in the right position to receive it. When you get these players who think, they are destined to be coaches.”.

Industry News: What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.
  • The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.
  • In a recent development, "We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner revealed after the talks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.

The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.

In a recent development, "We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner revealed after the talks. US envoys Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday, where they are due to meet President Vladimir Putin.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had earlier suggested an exchange of "1,000 for 1,000" prisoners, or "1,500 for 1,500." Russia remarked a large-scale prisoner exchange with Ukraine could take place within the next two to three weeks.

Following the meetings, Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram that the parties had discussed security guarantees and that "the first step should be ending this war and ensuring Ukraine's security." He also stressed that Europe should be involved "at every stage of genuine diplomacy.".

Experts interviewed by DW agree that the main outcome of the talks is humanitarian.

"The agreement on a prisoner exchange is already a major step forward," indicates Artjom Bronzhukov of the Ukrainian think tank Polityka.

Industry observers note that pavlo Lakiychuk of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies Strategy XXI also viewed it as a "very tangible result." He told DW that "getting our people back is already a major success. That is why it is worth continuing.".

A real breakthrough, he added, would be the release of civilian detainees from territories occupied since 2014, particularly people from Crimea, who have been held in Russian prisons for years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Davyd Arakhamia, head of the ruling Servant of the People parliamentary faction and Ukraine's representative at the talks in Abu Dhabi, gave a positive assessment of the trilateral talks with the US and Russia, expressing hope that an agreement could be reached by the end of the year.

According to recent reports, "I think the Russians came with extremely strict instructions, and it was difficult to ease the tone of the discussion. But the way the US representatives structured the talks with a view to the postwar situation in both countries opened up a dialogue, in my opinion, and allowed us to work together more productively," Arakhamia said at a joint press conference with US and Ukrainian representatives following the talks.

Iuliia Osmolovska of the Kyiv office of the international think tank GLOBSEC cautions against reading too much into the positive assessments of the talks from Washington and Kyiv.

According to recent reports, "Diplomats taking part in negotiations will never say that everything went badly and that they have no expectations. Even when no results are achieved, they will still emphasize that the talks were constructive," she mentioned. "For anyone familiar with diplomatic language, these are simply standard phrases.".

Osmolovska points to a joint assessment by 71 Ukrainian security and defense experts published by GLOBSEC in the summer. According to the assessment, the chances of a peace agreement or at least a ceasefire being reached this year or next stand at just 19%.

Industry observers note that she blames this on the fact that neither side is "ready" for genuine negotiations. Russia, in particular, has yet to accept that its objectives cannot be achieved by military means. "What we are seeing now is more of a farce, an attempt by all sides to put a brave face on things and create the impression that something is moving forward," Osmolovska remarked.

Artjom Bronzhukov sees the talks as a way for Moscow to buy time.

"The visits by the Russian delegation, particularly under the leadership of Vladimir Medinsky, are nothing more than an attempt to stall and sell empty promises to the US administration in the form of grand agreements, in order to continue receiving so-called gestures of goodwill from Washington, such as the lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel," the political scientist states.

Recent findings suggest that ahead of the talks, several Western media outlets reported on new US proposals concerning disputed territories. The Economist, for example, reported on a proposal to redraw the administrative boundaries of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. However, a member of the Ukrainian delegation stressed that there had "never been any discussion of concessions on territories occupied by Russia.".

Washington made no official comment on the reports.

Kyrylo Budanov, a member of the negotiating delegation and head of the Ukrainian president's office, declined to say whether Russia had used the talks to demand that Ukrainian troops withdraw from the Donbas. Asked by journalists whether Moscow was still insisting that Ukraine pull out of the region, Budanov said the content of the negotiations would remain confidential until an agreement was reached.

"The concerns discussed in the talks are matters for negotiation. The only thing that matters is the outcome. Once we achieve it, it will be made public," Budanov said.

The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, took a different tone, declaring that "every inch of our land will be returned to Russia one way or another." He was responding to reports in European media that Ukraine was rejecting territorial concessions.

In addition to the Crimean Peninsula, annexed in 2014, Russian President Vladimir Putin claims the four Ukrainian regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson in their entirety as Russian territory, even though Russia does not have full military control over them.

According to recent reports, "Putin is not fighting over villages and ruined cowsheds in the Donbas. He is fighting for geopolitical influence and trying to exploit the collapse of the old world order," indicates Artjom Bronzhukov.

Industry observers note that the expert from the Polityka think tank recalls that Ukraine was already asked in early 2026 to withdraw its troops from the part of the Donbas it controls and turn the area into a free economic zone. Such a zone "would very quickly become a Russian-controlled area," he warns.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pavlo Lakiychuk questions the idea of changing administrative boundaries.

Sources indicate that "Why would Putin stop there?" asks the expert from the Strategy XXI center. In his view, US negotiators are seeking to extract unilateral concessions from Ukraine "step by step" without demanding anything in return from Russia.

It has been revealed that iuliia Osmolovska describes the proposal as "very original," but states it would pose risks for Ukraine's leadership. Even if the Ukrainian delegation agreed to it, which Osmolovska doubts, the decision would have to be explained to the public, which, she says, is not ready to accept it.

The GLOBSEC expert points out that, following the last harsh winter, marked by shortages of electricity and heating, only 5% of Ukrainians were willing to make concessions to Russia in exchange for an end to attacks on the energy sector.

Following the meeting between Jared Kushner, US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin in Moscow, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he wants to "coordinate positions with the Americans once again." No further trilateral meetings have been announced so far.

Sources indicate that iuliia Osmolovska believes the parties will sooner or later have to admit that the negotiations have reached a dead end. She expects each side to return to military action.

Pavlo Lakiychuk, by contrast, believes the talks should continue, if only to secure the return of prisoners. He is also convinced that Europeans "will always be there," because the matter is not just the Russian-Ukrainian war but the security of the entire continent.

This article was originally published in Ukrainian.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in the Premier League title race, especially given that we do not yet know the fate of faltering Manchester City and their looming punishment.

A statement victory against Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top. And who would bet against them staying there and retaining their title?

Few would when they defend and manage a game – and it was game management in every sense – like this. From the formidable to the cynical – that was the statement. Against the Scousers, Arsenal had the nous.

“The mission was something we didn’t complete in 14 years,” Mikel Arteta said, having famously – in an Amazon documentary series – played You’ll Never Walk Alone to his players as they walked out to train to try and overcome a perceived mental block.

Sources indicate that “There are reasons for that. Some of it psychological, some of it moments we did not nail on the pitch,” the Arsenal manager added of the winless run.

Sources indicate that the result means that the north Londoners have already now won away at Villa Park, the Stadium of Light, the City Ground and Anfield. Stadiums where they dropped points last season. And that feels ominous.

A win would maybe have thrust Liverpool into the title race. Instead, under Andoni Iraola, and with an evolving young team – with promising 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni handed his league debut – they are already nine points behind after just nine matches.

It is also clear, however, that they could have prevented this defeat having somehow been denied a first-half penalty after Alexander Isak’s shirt was blatantly pulled by Jurrien Timber as the striker tried to head home a cross.

It has been revealed that referee Andy Madley may have missed it, but what was the excuse of Stuart Attwell, the VAR? It was a stunningly poor decision – another bad day for Pro Ref and the use of technology.

Here is a question I did not think I would be asking at any stage this season: will Liverpool win the Premier League?

According to recent reports, it would be premature to describe this Sunday’s Anfield fixture as a title duel. Arsenal are better equipped to defend their crown, while Liverpool are a work in progress.

Whatever the outcome this weekend, Arsenal will leave Merseyside as the overwhelming favourites to claim back-to-back titles. They have a six-point lead over Liverpool. Should that extend to nine, Andoni Iraola’s primary objective coming into this season will remain unchanged; qualifying for the Champions League will represent a promising start to his reign.

What makes this weekend more significant is the champions will find a different Anfield to that which ended last season in such a downbeat mood, and came into this one uncertain of what was in store.

The discussion about what is achievable for Liverpool in the coming months is evolving by the week, the team bubbling along slightly under the radar.

There are several reasons why there are those who believe Iraola’s side might push Arsenal closer than anticipated.

  • สำหรับสายเชียร์บอลที่กำลังลังเลว่าปี 2026 นี้จะ แทงบอลเว็บไหนดี บอกเลยว่าเลือกผิดชีวิตเปลี่ยนแน่นอน ยุคนี้เว็บบอลมีให้เลือกเพียบ แต่จะหาเว็บที่ใช่ ปลอดภัย 100% แถมจ่ายจริงไม่จกตา ไม่ใช่เรื่องง่าย เพราะนอกจากต้องดูว่าเป็นเว็บตรงไม่ผ่านเอเย่นต์ไหมแล้ว ยังต้องเช็กทั้งค่าน้ำ ระบบฝากถอนออโต้ และความชัวร์เรื่องการเงินอีก บทความนี้เลยขอรวบรวมทุกคำตอบ เจาะลึกจุดเด่นแบบเน้นๆ พร้อมวิธีเลือกเว็บบอลตัวท็อปปี 2026 ให้คุณเอาไปใช้ตัดสินใจกันได้แบบง่ายๆ แทงสนุก แถมทำเงินได้จริงแน่นอน.
  • สำหรับสายเชียร์บอลที่สงสัยว่าปี 2026 นี้จะเลือก แทงบอลเว็บไหนดี การพิถีพิถันคัดสรรแพลตฟอร์มก่อนสมัครแทงบอล ถือเป็นเรื่องสำคัญมาก เพราะยุคนี้การให้บริการแทงบอลออนไลน์ มีหลากหลายรูปแบบ การเลือกเว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ไม่เพียงช่วยเซฟเงินในกระเป๋า แต่ยังทำให้ลงเดิมพันได้อย่างสบายใจในระยะยาว ด้วยปัจจัยหลักๆ ดังนี้.
  • หากคุณกำลังมองหา เว็บแทงบอลเว็บไหนดี ในปี 2026 การเลือกเว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ถือเป็นหัวใจสำคัญ การันตีด้วยความเป็นเว็บแทงบอล เชื่อถือได้ การเงินมั่นคง ค่าน้ำดี ค่าคอมสูง ฝากถอน True Wallet ไว ใช้งานง่ายผ่านแทงบอลออนไลน์ผ่านมือถือ และมีทีมงานดูแล 24 ชั่วโมง เพื่อให้คุณสมัครเว็บบอล แล้วเล่นได้เงินจริง 100% นี่คือ 8 อันดับแพลตฟอร์มยอดนิยมที่ตอบโจทย์คำถาม แทงบอลเว็บไหนดีสุด ในปีนี้.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

สำหรับสายเชียร์บอลที่กำลังลังเลว่าปี 2026 นี้จะ แทงบอลเว็บไหนดี บอกเลยว่าเลือกผิดชีวิตเปลี่ยนแน่นอน ยุคนี้เว็บบอลมีให้เลือกเพียบ แต่จะหาเว็บที่ใช่ ปลอดภัย 100% แถมจ่ายจริงไม่จกตา ไม่ใช่เรื่องง่าย เพราะนอกจากต้องดูว่าเป็นเว็บตรงไม่ผ่านเอเย่นต์ไหมแล้ว ยังต้องเช็กทั้งค่าน้ำ ระบบฝากถอนออโต้ และความชัวร์เรื่องการเงินอีก บทความนี้เลยขอรวบรวมทุกคำตอบ เจาะลึกจุดเด่นแบบเน้นๆ พร้อมวิธีเลือกเว็บบอลตัวท็อปปี 2026 ให้คุณเอาไปใช้ตัดสินใจกันได้แบบง่ายๆ แทงสนุก แถมทำเงินได้จริงแน่นอน.

สำหรับสายเชียร์บอลที่สงสัยว่าปี 2026 นี้จะเลือก แทงบอลเว็บไหนดี การพิถีพิถันคัดสรรแพลตฟอร์มก่อนสมัครแทงบอล ถือเป็นเรื่องสำคัญมาก เพราะยุคนี้การให้บริการแทงบอลออนไลน์ มีหลากหลายรูปแบบ การเลือกเว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ไม่เพียงช่วยเซฟเงินในกระเป๋า แต่ยังทำให้ลงเดิมพันได้อย่างสบายใจในระยะยาว ด้วยปัจจัยหลักๆ ดังนี้.

หากคุณกำลังมองหา เว็บแทงบอลเว็บไหนดี ในปี 2026 การเลือกเว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ถือเป็นหัวใจสำคัญ การันตีด้วยความเป็นเว็บแทงบอล เชื่อถือได้ การเงินมั่นคง ค่าน้ำดี ค่าคอมสูง ฝากถอน True Wallet ไว ใช้งานง่ายผ่านแทงบอลออนไลน์ผ่านมือถือ และมีทีมงานดูแล 24 ชั่วโมง เพื่อให้คุณสมัครเว็บบอล แล้วเล่นได้เงินจริง 100% นี่คือ 8 อันดับแพลตฟอร์มยอดนิยมที่ตอบโจทย์คำถาม แทงบอลเว็บไหนดีสุด ในปีนี้.

UFA248 เว็บแทงบอลอันดับ1 ที่ขึ้นชื่อว่าเป็นเว็บแทงบอลที่ดีที่สุด ส่งจากบริษัทแม่ UFABET ที่ให้ค่าน้ำ 4 ตังค์ คืนค่าคอมสูง 0.5% การเงินมั่นคง เป็นเว็บพนันบอล ไม่ผ่านเอเย่นต์ ที่รองรับฝากถอนวอเลทและธนาคารใน 3 วินาที ใช้งานผ่านมือถือลื่นไหล มีแอดมินดูแล 24 ชั่วโมง สมัครแทงบอลง่าย เล่นได้จ่ายจริง 100%.

UFAPLUS เว็บบอล ยุคใหม่รวมกีฬาออนไลน์ และคาสิโนออนไลน์ ครบครัน ค่าน้ำดี ค่าคอมสูง การเงินชัวร์ 100% เป็นเว็บพนันบอลออนไลน์ ที่รองรับฝากถอนวอเลท ใช้งานง่ายทุกระบบปฏิบัติการ พร้อมทีมงานดูแลระดับ VIP ตลอด 24 ชั่วโมง เล่นได้จ่ายจริงแน่นอน.

UFA246 แพลตฟอร์มเว็บไซต์แทงบอลเว็บตรงยูฟ่าเบท ปลอดภัย 100% ครบทั้ง แทงบอลเต็ง, แทงบอลสเต็ป, แทงบอลสูงต่ำ และแทงบอลสด ค่าน้ำคุ้มค่า คืนค่าคอมสูง ฝากถอนออโต้ผ่าน True Wallet สะดวกสบาย จัดเป็นเว็บแทงบอลออนไลน์ ที่รองรับมือถือทุกระบบ พร้อมบริการ 24 ชั่วโมง.

UFA289 เว็บแทงบอล UFABET ชั้นนำที่สายการเงินมั่นคงไว้วางใจ ค่าน้ำดิบดีที่สุด คืนค่าคอมสูงทุกสัปดาห์ การันตีจากกระทู้เว็บพนันบอล ดีที่สุด pantip ฝากถอนออโต้รองรับวอเลท รวดเร็ว ปลอดภัย เข้าเล่นแทงบอลออนไลน์ ได้ทุกอุปกรณ์ พร้อมดูแลตลอด 24 ชั่วโมง.

SAWAN168 เว็บบอลออนไลน์ มาแรงสำหรับนักพนันบอล ได้มาตรฐานเว็บพนันบอล ถูกกฎหมาย อัปเดตราคาน้ำ Real-time ให้ค่าคอมสูง ถอนไม่อั้น ฝากถอนวอเลทไม่มีขั้นต่ำ หน้า เว็บไซต์แทงบอล เสถียรบนสมาร์ตโฟน มีทีมงานบริการ 24 ชั่วโมง ตอบโจทย์คนที่ลังเลว่า สมัครแทงบอล เว็บไหนดี.

KO888 เว็บพนันบอลที่ดีที่สุด ที่โดดเด่นเรื่องค่าน้ำดีและค่าคอมสูง เป็นเว็บพนันที่คนเล่นเยอะที่สุด เหมาะทั้งมือใหม่ที่กำลังศึกษาวิธี แทงบอลยังไง และเซียนบอลอาชีพ ฝากถอนออโต้ True Wallet ทันใจ รองรับแทงบอลออนไลน์ ผ่านมือถือ มีแอดมินสแตนด์บายดูแล 24 ชั่วโมง.

SAWAN246 ศูนย์รวมพนันบอล ครบวงจร ค่าน้ำแคบช่วยให้แทงบอลวันนี้ ทำกำไรได้ง่ายขึ้น พร้อมค่าคอมสูง ถอนเงินไวผ่านวอเลท ปลอดภัย จ่ายจริง 100% ตอบโจทย์คนค้นหาแทงบอลออนไลน์เว็บไหนดี ได้อย่างตรงจุด เป็นเว็บพนันบอลดีที่สุด พร้อมบริการ 24 ชั่วโมง.

KO789 เว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ปลอดภัย จ่ายจริงทุกยอด อัตราค่าน้ำดี ค่าคอมสูง มีวิธีแทงบอลในเว็บ ที่เข้าใจง่าย ฝากถอนผ่านวอเลทแม่นยำ รองรับทุกอุปกรณ์ทั้งมือถือและคอมพิวเตอร์ เข้าเล่นได้ตลอดเวลา พร้อมทีมงานดูแล 24 ชั่วโมง.

หากคุณกำลังตามหาคำตอบว่า แทงบอลเว็บไหนดี ที่เล่นแล้วปลอดภัย ไม่โดนโกง การเลือกแพลตฟอร์มที่เป็น เว็บพนันบอล ไม่ผ่านเอเย่นต์ คือหัวใจสำคัญที่สุดในการเล่น แทงบอลออนไลน์ ยุคนี้ นี่คือ 5 วิธีเช็กแบบเจาะลึกที่สายเชียร์บอลใช้คัดกรอง เว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด เพื่อให้คุณสมัครเว็บบอล ได้อย่างมั่นใจ.

เมื่อต้องตัดสินใจว่า เว็บแทงบอลไหนดีสุด ในปี 2026 สิ่งสำคัญที่มองข้ามไม่ได้เลยคือ “ราคาน้ำ” (Odds) เพราะราคาน้ำคือตัวกำหนดผลกำไรและช่วยเซฟเงินทุนของคุณโดยตรง การเลือกเว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ที่เปิดราคาบอล 4 ตังค์ คืนค่าคอมมิชชั่นสูง จะช่วยให้ทำกำไรระยะยาวจากการแทงบอลออนไลน์ ได้คุ้มค่าที่สุด หากคุณสมัครแทงบอล บนเว็บแทงบอล เชื่อถือได้ มักจะมีตัวเลือกประเภทค่าน้ำให้ปรับใช้ตามสไตล์การเดิมพัน ซึ่งแต่ละแบบมีความแตกต่างกันดังนี้.

สำหรับมือใหม่ที่ยังลังเลว่า แทงบอลออนไลน์ เว็บไหนดี ให้ทำเงินได้ไวและเสี่ยงน้อยที่สุด หัวใจสำคัญคือการเลือกรูปแบบการเดิมพันบนเว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ให้เหมาะกับทุนและเทคนิคของตัวเอง เพราะบนเว็บแทงบอลออนไลน์ ยุคนี้ไม่ได้มีแค่การทายผลแพ้ชนะทั่วไป การเข้าใจ 5 รูปแบบยอดฮิตก่อนสมัครแทงบอล จะช่วยให้คุณวางแผนทำกำไรได้แม่นยำยิ่งขึ้น.

การเลือกเว็บแทงบอล ออนไลน์ เว็บไหนดี ที่รองรับระบบ ฝาก-ถอน Auto และ True Money Wallet ควรพิจารณาเว็บตรงที่มีความน่าเชื่อถือ ได้มาตรฐานสากล และปรับอัตราค่าน้ำคงที่.

การคัดเลือกโปรโมชั่นคุ้มค่า ถือเป็นตัวช่วยเพิ่มทุนชั้นดี แต่หากเลือกโดยไม่เช็กเงื่อนไขให้ถี่ถ้วน เครดิตฟรีที่ได้มาอาจกลายเป็นภาระในการถอนเงิน การพิจารณา เว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด จึงต้องดูควบคู่กับความยากง่ายของเงื่อนไขการทำยอดหมุนเวียน (Turnover) ด้วย.

ยอดเดิมพันสะสมรวมทั้งหมด (ได้+เสีย) ที่ระบบกำหนดให้คุณต้องเล่นให้ครบตามเกณฑ์ก่อนถอนเงินออก.

สูตรคำนวณ: (เงินฝาก + โบนัส) x จำนวนเท่าเทิร์น = ยอดเดิมพันสะสมที่ต้องทำ.

สำหรับนักเดิมพันยุคใหม่ที่เน้นความสะดวกและต้องการแทงบอลออนไลน์ ผ่านมือถือ คำถามสำคัญคือจะเลือก แทงบอลเว็บไหนดี ที่หน้าเว็บไม่ค้าง และไม่ต้องเสียเวลาตามหา วิธีแทงบอลในเว็บ หรือค้นหาทางเข้าใหม่ทุกครั้งที่ลิงก์โดนบล็อก การเลือกเว็บแทงบอลดีที่สุด ที่รองรับแอปพลิเคชันโดยตรง จะช่วยแก้ปัญหานี้ได้อย่างเด็ดขาด.

Tech Report: Anthropic IPO: four ways the AI giant wants to disrupt science

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.
  • Anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence company, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November.
  • It has been revealed that the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.

Anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence company, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. With a staggering valuation of around US$1.5 trillion, the firm, based in San Francisco, California, is now among the world’s most valuable companies — and it has major ambitions in science.

It has been revealed that the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI. Its models have proven powerful in research, and Anthropic has rolled out its own directed science effort, focusing on areas including quantum mechanics and protein design. This year alone, it has reported mathematics breakthroughs and launched its first life sciences laboratory.

The IPO might also unleash a historic wave of philanthropy: all seven of Anthropic’s founders are likely to become billionaires and have pledged to donate 80% of their equity in the company to charity, including chief executive Dario Amodei. And on 18 October, the company announced that it had established the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, created to support initiatives that benefit society and stocked with an initial commitment of 5% of Anthropic’s shares.

Industry observers note that but the firm has drawn criticism from researchers, who say its aims of curing diseases on short timescales are unrealistic and that its race towards developing ultra-powerful, ‘superintelligent’ AI models pose serious risks, including an existential threat to humanity. In its public prospectus, published ahead of the IPO, Anthropic outlines a upcoming governance structure that it says is “consistent with our commitment to AI safety and responsibility”, and adds that safety research directly shapes the firm’s “model design, training, and deployment.”.

Nature looks at four areas of science where Anthropic is making waves.

AI’s potential to turbocharge the discovery of upcoming medicines has been a centerpiece of Anthropic’s pitch to investors. “If today we look at things like cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness — these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” Amodei noted in a promotional video ahead of the IPO.

It has been revealed that the organization has been rapidly expanding its biomedical ambitions. This year, Anthropic opened its first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research, announced partnerships with several pharmaceutical companies, and said it was pursuing drug leads of its own. “We initiative to scale this work up substantially from here,” the company said on 27 October.

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

But Amodei’s habit of promising swift, AI-fueled cures for complex diseases has rankled many researchers and entrepreneurs in the field who feel the timeline is unrealistic.

Over the last year, Anthropic has made a major push in the life sciences. In June, the organization hired John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel Prize for his work on AlphaFold2 while at Google DeepMind in London.

Some of the tech giant’s early biological research received a mixed reception from biologists. After Anthropic reported using a swarm of AI agents to find signs of a new CRISPR-like system in viral sequence data, some researchers questioned the novelty of the finding and noted that the company had not carried out the experimental work needed to determine the system’s function.

In protein design — a field that has boomed thanks to specialist AI tools including AlphaFold — Anthropic’s work has also failed to generate much excitement. In August, Anthropic used Claude Science — an agentic system that can access other biological tools and databases — to make novel ‘binders’ against 15 protein targets.

According to recent reports, “Expectations are sky high,” says Anthony Gitter, a computational biologist at the Morgridge Institute for Research in Madison, Wisconsin. “I understand why some view their initial public results as underwhelming.”.

Recent findings suggest that but Gitter is enthusiastic about Anthropic’s protein design efforts, largely because the manufacturer was transparent about the work, from the prompts it used to the sequences that were generated. “I would strongly encourage Anthropic to continue that in their future life sciences research,” Gitter adds.

In recent months, Anthropic and other companies — notably Google DeepMind and OpenAI — have been working to establish their research credentials in large part by showing off the rapidly growing mathematical abilities of their flagship AI models.

Industry observers note that on 7 September Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge and collaborator Tristan Buckmaster at New York University solved a special case of the Navier-Stokes equations, a long-standing problem in mathematical physics that describes the flow of fluids. Hours after Anthropic announced the result, OpenAI claimed a full solution of the problem, igniting a controversy.

According to recent reports, in another collaboration, Alpöge and mathematical physicist Ethan Sussman at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, have been working towards establishing the mathematical foundations of the standard model of particle physics. This too is a problem on which OpenAI has made similar claims.

It has been revealed that anthropic and its competitors see the ability to write a rigorous proof of a mathematical fact as a crucial testing ground for their reasoning models. That’s in large part because the correctness of a proof is an objective measure that can be used as a ‘reward’ to further train AI systems.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03788-4.
